items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: But I am proud to say from that time on I said I’ve got to try to learn to articulate on the clarinet like he does on the alto.

ctx.x: Your first experience in bebop, where did that take place? Back in New York?

Yeah. Back in New York. I had not worked with Charlie Shavers at the time but we knew Charlie pretty well and met him on Broadway. When I say “we,” Dodo Marmarosa, who was quite a piano player. I would say at fourteen years old he was one of the best in the world, jazz piano player, who also recorded with Bird and was on all of the bands that I’ve played with including Tommy Dorsey. He was with Artie Shaw as well. Dodo Marmarosa. Artie loved his playing. But he and I ran into Charlie Shavers. And Charlie Shavers…
It takes an awful lot of facility to pull that off.

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Yeah. That was really intimidating. Bird had, Bird was great though, he was congenial, nice person…
So the first time you met him you played together?

We played together, yeah. Of course, there was one time that he; it was customary, I think, to play games with playing, too. Or stump the experts as they say because we had one session together and we had, he said, “What do you want to play?” And I said, “I want to play All the Things You Are” because I had been wood-shedding All the Things You Are and I think it was A-flat, concert A-flat. And Bird says “Great, lets do it in D” and he went right into it, you see. [laughter] And my head started spinning and even…
